ledger.note: 1753: the Al Madhkur of Bushehr take Bahrain. 'In 1753, the Al Madhkur family, based in Bushire, occupied Bahrain'; they 'ruled Bahrain in the name of Persia and paid allegiance to Karim Khan Zand' (the Bahrain page: 'the Huwala clan of Nasr Al-Madhkur invaded on behalf of Zand leader Karim Khan Zand', which 'restored direct Iranian rule'). The Nasr Al-Madhkur page: Bahrain had been controlled by the sheikh of Asalu, his first invasion in the second half of 1751 failed, and 'in 1753, an attack from Bandar Ganaveh forced Mir Naser to return to Bandar Rig, allowing Nasr Al-Madhkur to take the island'.

17 May 1783: war between Nasr Al-Madhkur and the Bani Utbah. 'On 17 May 1783, war broke out between the Zubarah-based Al Bin Ali Bani Utbah clan and the army of Nasr Al-Madhkur'; the History of Bahrain page dates the war to 1782 ('historians disagree on whether the invasion of Bahrain came in 1782 or 1783') and the battle of Zubarah to 1782.

28 July 1783: the conquest is complete. 'the invasion of Bahrain was completed on 28 July 1783'; Ahmed Al Fateh defeated Nasr Al-Madhkur outside Manama, and Persian attempts to retake the island failed in 1783 and 1785.
28 July 1783: Al Madhkur rule ends and the Al Khalifa state begins. The islands pass to the Bani Utbah (Al Khalifa), who rule Bahrain from Zubarah until they move to Bahrain in 1797.

notes: Written by me-10-d on 2026-10-25 from three pages (budget up to 5). STATE: Cliopatria's 'Bahrain' (1757-1845) shares Wikidata Q398 with 'Kingdom of Bahrain' (1973-2024). They are NOT read as one state here. The 1757-1782 shape is the Persian-dependent Bahrain of the Al Madhkur (1753-1783); the continuous Bahraini state under the Al Khalifa starts in 1783 and is the house-of-khalifa dossier, which this agent also owns, and whose Cliopatria row runs 1783-1894; the Kingdom of Bahrain (me-10-l) should follow it. The three dossiers (bahrain, house-of-khalifa, kingdom-of-bahrain) are one story and the colour agent may want one hue for the last two. CLIOPATRIA ROWS 1820-1829, 1840-1841 and 1842-1845 (72,705 km2) are the Eastern Province of Saudi Arabia, not Bahrain; they overlap the Emirate of Diriyah's 1819 shape cell for cell. Verdict wrong for all three; the archipelago in those years is the House of Khalifa row (881.5 km2). WHO HELD AL-AHSA, QATIF AND DAMMAM IN 1820-1845 is not answered by any page opened (the History of Bahrain page says only that Faisal bin Turki took Al-Ahsa and Saihat in the 1840s and the Egyptians took the peninsula in 1830): a task for the Emirate of Nejd / Muhammad Ali dynasty dossiers. PERSIAN TIE: the Zand dossier records the Al Madhkur as a Zand vassal 1753-1783 (vassal_start/end, counterpart 'bahrain'); the Nasr Al-Madhkur page says he 'declared independence' of Bushehr in January 1751 and does not describe a tribute to Karim Khan. Nothing in this ledger repeats those events because the schema puts a vassal relation in the suzerain's ledger. NOT DONE: the 1717 and 1738 Omani invasions and the 1736 Persian invasion (History of Bahrain) precede the dossier and are not entered.
